title: UP man rapes GF, kills her after taking sexual stimulant drug at hotel on birthday
content: A 23-year-old man allegedly booked a hotel room and consumed a sexual stimulant drug. He then raped his 22-year-old girlfriend and murdered her when she resisted. The woman, a Dalit, was returning to her village for Raksha Bandhan. Police recovered the victim's mobile phone and stimulant tablets from the accused. An FIR was registered under murder and rape sections of the BNS.

title: 10 'Toy trains' cancelled on Kalka-Shimla heritage route after track left hanging
content: Ten trains on the Kalka-Shimla heritage line were cancelled after heavy rain damaged the track. Soil slippage between Koti and Gumman stations left a section of the track suspended. This disruption inconvenienced many passengers who had booked tickets in advance. Meanwhile, rainfall across Himachal Pradesh led to sixty-four road closures. The state has suffered significant losses and over one hundred deaths this monsoon.

title: 1,300 days, 36 innings, no 100: How Babar’s Test century drought became a long story
content: Babar Azam's quest for a Test century continues as he remains without a hundred since December 2022. Over the course of seventeen Tests and thirty-six innings, he has frequently come close with several fifties but has yet to convert those into three-figure scores. His challenges surged notably in 2024, despite a temporary revival in South Africa.

title: US uranium output triples as nuclear fuel becomes a defence priority
content: United States uranium production more than tripled in 2025, reaching its highest level since 2017.  Domestic mines supplied only a small share of uranium required by the country's nuclear sector.  Most supplies continued to come from overseas, highlighting a significant dependence.  The United States has been trying to rebuild its domestic uranium enrichment capabilities.  Major investments aim to reduce reliance on foreign suppliers and strengthen the nuclear fuel chain.

title: Michael Dell shares a 'special note' for COO as he completes 39 years
content: Dell COO Jeff Clarke marked thirty-nine years with the technology company.  This milestone coincides with Dell's major 'One Dell Way' transformation initiative.  The company is consolidating multiple applications and systems into a single enterprise platform.  This comprehensive change aims to simplify processes and enhance data flow across departments.  The transformation is designed to prepare Dell for an AI-driven business environment.

title: Himachal identifies 67 vulnerable glacial lakes, early warning systems planned for 4
content: The state is monitoring the identified lakes through satellite imagery and other scientific data to detect changes that could increase the risk of glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs), while technical solutions are being explored to install sensors and transmit real-time information from locations where conventional communication networks are unavailable.

title: 417 FC wickets, just 3 Tests: The forgotten story of Subhash Gupte’s brother Baloo
content: Baloo Gupte, a talented leg-spinner, had a short-lived international career, featuring in just three Tests for India after his brother Subhash was sidelined. Despite only capturing three wickets during this brief period, Baloo's prowess shone brightly in domestic cricket, where he amassed over 400 first-class wickets, showcasing a talent that unfortunately didn't lead to more extensive Test success.

title: 'Bill Gates wrong about robot tax': Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
content: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang disagrees with Bill Gates' robot tax proposal. Huang believes AI will create more jobs overall, not fewer. He suggests companies with increased productivity tend to hire more people. Huang sees a future of reindustrialization with demand for skilled labor. This new economic era will create many jobs across various sectors.

title: NEET row: Youth Congress protests at Bengaluru BJP office, demands Shah's resignation
content: Karnataka Youth Congress workers were detained while protesting alleged NEET exam irregularities. Demonstrators gathered near the BJP office, raising slogans against the central government. Police detained the protesters who had assembled at the spot and released them later. The Youth Congress alleged police used a lathi-charge to disperse its members. The organization demanded the resignation of Union Home Minister Amit Shah.

title: Javagal Srinath spotted in Bengaluru Metro, wins praise for simplicity
content: A captivating photograph of Javagal Srinath riding the Bengaluru Metro has caught the public's eye. Carrying his luggage and blending in with fellow commuters, Srinath's humble demeanor continues to win the hearts of fans. This isn't a first for him; his down-to-earth lifestyle often earns admiration. Meanwhile, he remains active in cricket as an ICC match referee, showcasing a perfect balance between stardom and simplicity.

title: Amid software fears, Anthropic CEO says: ‘We’re not here to destroy anyone’
content: Anthropic's CEO assures investors that AI will not dismantle enterprise software companies.  He views AI expansion as a positive, collaborative evolution for the technology sector.  Wall Street experienced sell-offs after an AI announcement, but software firms have recovered.  Salesforce reported strong growth and client retention, deepening its AI integration.  Concerns persist regarding data security and enterprise autonomy with AI providers.

title: How to avoid rental disputes: Delhi Police plans awareness session for Northeast tenants
content: Delhi Police will host an awareness program next week for Northeast residents.  The event will focus on rental agreements and security deposit issues.  Tenants will learn about their rights and responsibilities regarding rent.  Police will widely circulate advisories with community leaders' help.  This initiative aims to prevent and resolve landlord-tenant disputes effectively.

title: Kabul, Kashmir, Mumbai, Pahalgam: Hafiz Saeed’s deadly four-decade terror trail
content: India has formally charged Hafiz Muhammad Saeed, the founder of Lashkar-e-Taiba, in connection with a new case of terrorism. The Mumbai Police have initiated proceedings for a trial in absentia, highlighting the legacy of LeT across various phases. Originating from the Afghan jihad in the 1980s, the organization has transitioned from focusing on Kashmir insurgency to embracing a wider range of terror operations.

title: Babar Azam fails again! Ex-Pakistan cricketer calls coaches ‘poison for the game’
content: Babar Azam's Test performance struggles escalated at Lord's, where he could only manage six runs. Former cricketer Mohammad Yousuf voiced strong criticism towards the coaching staff, labeling them as detrimental to player improvement. He argues that Pakistan's dismal overseas record, compounded by frequent leadership changes, amplifies the pressure, with the team having lost nine of its last ten away games.

title: Vivek On Postpartum Struggle: Actor says depression is real; links it to Divyanka’s recovery
content: Vivek Dahiya candidly addressed the often-overlooked challenges of postpartum depression, emphasizing the physical and hormonal shifts many mothers face. He highlighted the supportive journey of his wife, Divyanka Tripathi, as she embraced her evolving body post-childbirth. Together, they are navigating the ups and downs of parenthood, finding joy in the daily lessons and deepening their bond during this beautiful new chapter of their lives.

title: Bullion watch: What will shape gold, silver prices? Fed bets, US jobs data in focus
content: Throughout September, gold and silver prices are likely to remain under pressure. Critical influences on trading will stem from forthcoming US employment data releases. Traders should be alert to how central bank anticipations and persistent geopolitical tensions will steer market dynamics. Special attention will be given to non-farm payrolls and unemployment rates, as market players speculate on possible shifts in Federal Reserve policy.

title: 'Frustrated' elderly father, friend kill schizophrenic son in Delhi
content: A father and his friend were arrested for allegedly killing his son in Kalindi Kunj. The 64-year-old father claimed his schizophrenic son had become aggressive and unmanageable. Investigators found the victim's body with head injuries and signs of strangulation. The accused lured the victim to an abandoned container before assaulting him. Police recovered the murder weapon and bloodstained clothing from the scene.

title: ‘Identify your real enemy’: Khamenei urges Gulf rulers to unite, defend each other
content: Iran's Supreme Leader urged Gulf rulers to identify their real enemy and confront it. He also called for Muslim unity and mutual defense against external threats. The message comes amid ongoing war and significant economic pressure on Iran. Iranian President dismissed speculation about the leader's health, stating he is healthy. Diplomacy and defense remain Iran's complementary approach to national interests.

title: 7 bodies swept into Gandak river in UP's Maharajganj, Kushinagar amid Nepal floods
content: Seven unidentified bodies have been recovered from the Gandak river in Uttar Pradesh. Devastating floods in Nepal caused a sharp rise in the river's water flow. Officials are working to identify the deceased individuals found in the water. Bodies were discovered in Maharajganj and Kushinagar districts by villagers and SSB personnel. Efforts are ongoing to manage the situation and identify the recovered victims.

title: Delhi tightens fire safety rules: What property owners, developers need to know
content: In an effort to bolster city safety, new fire safety regulations have been implemented for buildings in Delhi. These updated guidelines, part of the Unified Building Bye-Laws, encompass eighteen crucial categories, including provision for fire engine access and secured exits. Additionally, structures are now required to maintain emergency power and continuous monitoring systems, all in response to recent fire incidents that highlighted the need for stronger protections.

title: 11 Slams, No 25th Yet: Can Djokovic finally end his Grand Slam drought at US Open?
content: At the 2026 US Open, Novak Djokovic eyes his remarkable 25th Grand Slam victory. With eight major semi-finals or better since 2023, he remains a formidable contender. This time, he benefits from a favourable draw, as young rivals Alcaraz and Sinner hold the spotlight. With Sinner out and Alcaraz recovering from an injury, Djokovic finds this moment significant, especially at the age of 39, for his potential final triumph.

title: From strange worlds to rare planets: Nasa’s Roman Telescope begins its cosmic hunt
content: Nasa's new Roman Space Telescope has launched on a mission to explore distant planets.  This observatory will search for dark matter and dark energy across the universe.  It is expected to discover thousands of new planets and billions of galaxies.  The telescope's wide field of view surpasses Hubble's capabilities significantly.  Roman will build upon the discoveries of Webb and Hubble observatories.

title: Iran war creates two front defence dilemma for US against China and Russia
content: The ongoing conflict in the Middle East has severely depleted US missile and air-defense stockpiles, leaving global defense capabilities compromised. Taiwan's defense posture against China experiences added uncertainty due to these shortages. Additionally, limited air-defense interceptor supplies hinder support for Ukraine, suggesting a lengthy and challenging replenishment process for these advanced weapons that could undermine readiness for years to come.

title: ‘Violation of HC order won't be tolerated’: Agnimitra Paul on FIR against Mamata

Police allege the program exceeded permitted timings and caused disruptions.  Ministers criticized Banerjee for disrespecting constitutional institutions and the judiciary.  The investigation will examine the roles of all individuals involved.

title: Istanbul to host first committee meeting of Turkey-Saudi-Pak defence alliance
content: Top officials from Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan met in Istanbul for a defense accord. This meeting follows the recent signing of the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement. The pact aims to enhance defense capabilities and interoperability among the three nations. Discussions will focus on collective deterrence and regional security issues. The alliance remains open to expansion with potential new members joining.

title: Karnataka IAS officer arrested in KPSC recruitment exam row

Reports indicate he failed to assist the ongoing inquiry into recruitment discrepancies. The Enforcement Directorate had earlier searched KPSC offices related to money laundering, with Gangwar's prior absence contributing to confusion in the case.

title: Watch: Captain Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s brave DRS call gets East Zone crucial wicket

His decisive action to challenge a caught behind appeal was a testament to his poise and growing prowess as a leader. East Zone's bowlers effectively maintained pressure throughout the match's initial session.

title: Odisha govt to transfer alimony from salaries of defaulting staffers to ex-wives
content: Odisha government will now deduct alimony directly from employee salaries. This order ensures timely financial support for estranged wives and children. Repeated complaints prompted the chief minister to take this stern stance. Court orders will now be enforced through automated salary deductions. This initiative aims to uphold judicial authority and ease family distress.

title: Bengaluru girl, 5, fights for inclusion after family was once told it was karma
content: Aeny, a spirited five-year-old, embraces the challenge of learning to walk with her cane, embodying a remarkable spirit of determination. With her parents cheering her on, Aeny steps confidently into a world filled with adventures. While Bengaluru does provide some support, achieving true inclusivity in schools continues to be a significant hurdle, prompting families to advocate for acceptance and equal rights for all children with disabilities.

title: Hyderabad horror: 21-year-old nurse found dead with bleeding injuries on her face

content: The US Open presents a critical moment for Aryna Sabalenka as she defends her world number one title amidst a recent performance slump. Targeting her third consecutive championship, Sabalenka must rising pressures to stay ahead of potential challengers like Elena Rybakina. Her quest for victory will hinge on her consistency and mental strength in tough situations.

title: What will guide Dalal Street this week? GDP data, crude and more in focus
content: This week promises significant economic developments on Dalal Street with a flurry of data to analyze. India’s Q1 FY27 GDP stats are anticipated on August 31, giving insight into economic growth. The August PMI figures for the manufacturing and services sectors will be closely watched as well. Furthermore, the US non-farm payrolls, released on September 4, is likely to steer expectations regarding the Federal Reserve's forthcoming decisions.

title: Chelsea land two-time world’s best goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez on three-year deal

Martinez, known for his vital contributions to Argentina's Copa America and World Cup victories, is eager to bring his invaluable experience and winning mindset to help Chelsea secure major trophies.

title: Pregnant for 7 weeks, missing for 54 days: New twists in Punjabi influencer's death case

An autopsy indicated she was almost seven weeks pregnant when she died. Her mother has lodged a complaint naming two individuals as suspects, and police are now on a mission to locate and apprehend them.

title: India’s economy set for 7-7.2% growth in FY27 despite global headwinds: EY
content: India's economy is poised for significant growth in FY27, with forecasts suggesting an expansion between 7 and 7.2 percent. This anticipated surge in economic activity will be driven by strong domestic demand and government investment initiatives. Notably, manufacturing is showing an impressive rebound, although inflation poses a considerable threat by affecting wholesale prices. Meanwhile, challenges in the external sector hint at the need for effective import reduction measures.

title: Nepal floods expose stark contrast as China keeps tight lid on information
content: Catastrophic flash floods struck villages along the Nepal-China border after a glacier broke. Nepal's death toll reached 538, while China reported only five deaths. China's tight information control in Tibet hampers disaster assessment and rescue coordination efforts. Independent reporting from Tibet is severely restricted due to its sensitive status. The information vacuum obscures the full human cost and extent of destruction.

title: PM Modi conferred with Uzbekistan’s highest state honour

title: Iran war at 6 months: Who gained, who lost the most economically
